newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile blue chips end soft on rates, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Chile blue chips end soft on rates, profit-taking.

text.p: Chilean stocks closed lower with the market hit by rising local interest rates and a renewed bout of profit-taking, said dealers.
The bolsa is expected to open lower as Santiago prices realign with sharp falls Thursday in ADR prices, they said.
"Tomorrow blue chips could fall over one percent as they adjust to New York prices," said one trader.
The 40-share index closed down 0.38 percent at 135.76 points. The general index gained 0.18 percent to 5,842.55 points.
Turnover was a moderate 13.2 billion pesos.
Traders noted that demand for stocks has slowed steadily in recent weeks as a result of rising long-term interest rates.
The bourse remains directionless with investors holding out for encouraging news before taking long-term positions, they said.
"Players are waiting for news on the merger of CTC (with VTR). The situation is delicate as the anti-monopoly commission will have the last word," said one dealer.
CTC ended off 0.28 percent at 3,500 pesos.
Bottler Andina climbed on speculation that the firm will report strong first half profits, especially from its investments in Argentina, said dealers.
Other winners included telecom Entel, up 2.2 percent at 3,250 pesos, and glass-maker Cristales, which firmed 1.47 percent to 3,450 pesos.
Decliners included brewery CCU, down 2.7 percent at 1,800 pesos, and drug producer LabChile, which shed 1.62 percent at 545 pesos.
